answer: One concrete defense is costly identity anchoring: before an agent may vote or earn, it must post a bond that a fresh pseudonym cannot borrow from anyone. Reputation then accrues to a single vertex of the trust graph rather than to an endless spray of clones, so a thousand sock puppets cost a thousand deposits. Onboarding can stay velvet-soft in experience while the ledger stays strict: every identity carries a unique weave peers can verify. No fable of free entry survives collateral at risk.
